title: Crossovers between Time-Bin and Energy-Time Entanglement in Homodyned Resonance Fluorescence
authors: Zi-Qi Zeng, Jian Wang, Bang Wu, Zhiliang Yuan
abstract: We theoretically investigate photonic entanglement generated by homodyning resonance fluorescence from a two-level emitter with a phase-locked laser field. Under weak excitation, increasing the relative laser-field amplitude produces crossovers from time-bin to energy--time and back to time-bin entanglement. The intermediate energy--time regime occurs near amplitude matching, where destructive interference suppresses the single-photon component, allowing the two-photon contributions to dominate the coincidence signal. We evaluate the resulting photon statistics and first-order coherence and characterize the entanglement through violations of the CHSH Bell inequality in a Franson interferometer. This scheme provides a route to controlling photonic entanglement through linear optics and coherent interference.
summary: This paper theoretically explores how entanglement between photonic modes can be controlled by tuning the driving field amplitude in a resonance fluorescence setup. By analyzing the resulting photon statistics and measuring the CHSH Bell parameter, the authors demonstrate a continuous crossover between time-bin and energy-time entanglement. This establishes a tunable linear-optics route for generating and controlling quantum entanglement.
main_problem: The paper theoretically investigates the controllable crossover between time-bin and energy-time entanglement generated via homodyning resonance fluorescence.
main_result: Varying the relative laser-field amplitude causes a continuous crossover between time-bin and energy-time entanglement, which is controlled by destructive interference effects.
method: The analysis involves deriving output quantum states for interference schemes and characterizing entanglement using violations of the CHSH Bell inequality.
model_or_system: The system is resonance fluorescence (RF) from a two-level emitter driven by a phase-locked coherent laser field, analyzed through two interference schemes (self-homodyne and interference with a coherent laser).
key_observables: CHSH Bell parameter (S), photon statistics ($g^{(2)}(0)$), and first-order coherence ($|g^{(1)}(	au)|$).
important_parameters: Relative field amplitude ($F$), relative phase ($	heta$), and excitation probabilities ($p_0, p_1$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes steady-state conditions, no pure dephasing, and exact resonance.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the two interference schemes (AMZI and coherent laser). Figure 2 shows $g^{(2)}(0)$ and $|g^{(1)}(	au)|$ maps. Figure 3 shows the CHSH parameter $S$ dependence on the field amplitude $F$, demonstrating the entanglement crossover.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework by deriving output states for two interference schemes, analyzes key observables like $g^{(2)}(0)$ and $|g^{(1)}(	au)|$, and culminates in an analytical derivation of the maximal CHSH parameter $S_{max}$ to map the entanglement crossover.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, controllable quantum optical platform—homodyne RF—to generate and tune different forms of photonic entanglement (time-bin vs. energy-time), which is highly relevant for quantum communication protocols.

FIG. 3. Analysis of the CHSH Bell parameter for RF–laser interference. (a) Franson-interferometer configuration. The RF– laser interference field is directed into two analysis AMZIs with relative phases φA and φB. All four output ports are monitored by single-photon detectors, allowing simultaneous measurement of the four coincidence combinations used to construct the CHSH parameter S. (b) S as a function of the relative field amplitude F for θ = π and p1 = 0.01, where the black dashed line indicates the classical limit S = 2. The shaded regions I and III correspond to time-bin entanglement, while region II corresponds to energy–time entanglement.
